macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. jobs report strengthens case for December Fed rate hike
items.summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, well above expectations, while unemployment fell to 4.1% and annual wage growth reached 3.1%. Markets raised the implied probability of a quarter-point Fed rate increase at the December meeting to about 80%.

items.title: U.S. stocks rebound, but major indexes post weekly losses
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.3% Friday, the Nasdaq gained 1.1%, and the Dow fell 0.5%. Despite the rebound, the Nasdaq lost 3.4% for the week, the S&P 500 declined 2.7%, and the Dow fell 0.9%, amid continued concern about AI valuations and spending.

items.title: AI stocks stabilize after sharp sell-off
items.summary: Technology and AI-related shares recovered Friday after a severe sell-off linked to concerns about elevated valuations, data-center spending, and the policy implications of the U.S. midterm elections. Investors remain focused on whether AI infrastructure investment can generate sufficient profits and cash flow.

items.title: Investors turn to October inflation data for Fed signals
items.summary: Markets are awaiting the U.S. consumer-price report due Tuesday for evidence on whether inflation remains elevated enough to support another rate increase. Forecasts cited by market coverage point to a 0.2% monthly rise in core prices and a 2.7% annual core-inflation rate.

items.title: Australia raises interest rate to an 18-year high
items.summary: Australia’s central bank increased its benchmark interest rate to its highest level in 18 years in a split decision. Governor Michele Bullock signaled a wait-and-see stance on additional tightening, sending the Australian dollar lower.

items.title: Berkshire Hathaway reports lower profit and increased buybacks
items.summary: Berkshire Hathaway bought back $9.6 billion of its own shares as reported profits declined, making the company’s capital-allocation activity a notable corporate development during the latest earnings cycle.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds near $76,000 as ETF outflows continue
items.summary: Bitcoin traded above $76,000 after an earlier 5.2% 24-hour decline, while U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $411.9 million in net outflows. Ether, Solana and BNB posted modest gains, while XRP and Dogecoin declined.[8]

items.title: U.S. Treasury restricts MEXC Global’s access to U.S. financial system
items.summary: FinCEN issued an order barring U.S. financial institutions from transferring funds with MEXC Global, alleging the exchange facilitated at least $16 billion in transactions linked to sanctions evasion and cybercrime.[1]

items.title: European Commission forms cryptocurrency sanctions task force
items.summary: The European Commission established a cryptocurrency working group to address the use of digital assets to evade sanctions against Russia. The group is expected to coordinate enforcement with EU member states, Ukraine and the United Kingdom.[3]

items.title: Circle mints $250 million in USDC on Solana
items.summary: Circle’s USDC Treasury minted 250 million USDC on the Solana network, according to blockchain-monitoring data.[1]

items.title: Fidelity transfers approximately 27,000 ETH to Galaxy Digital
items.summary: Blockchain-monitoring data indicated that Fidelity transferred roughly 27,000 ETH, valued at about $60.27 million, to Galaxy Digital.[1]

items.title: Zcash activates NU7 upgrade and shortens block interval
items.summary: Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade, reducing the target block time from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.[9]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake launches
items.summary: A highly anticipated remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time officially launched this week after years of speculation about a revival of the classic game.

items.title: Silver Lake and Saudi PIF reportedly bid $25 billion for Unity
items.summary: A consortium led by Silver Lake and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund has reportedly offered to acquire Unity Software for about $25 billion. Unity is considering the proposal and has hired an investment bank to advise it, though no agreement had been reached as of November 6.

items.title: CRYMELIGHT releases on PS5 and Switch 2
items.summary: FURYU launched the roguelike action-adventure game CRYMELIGHT on PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2, while its Steam release was delayed amid unresolved review and approval issues.

items.title: GTA 6 PC release timing remains uncertain
items.summary: Rockstar has not announced PC or online launch details for Grand Theft Auto VI. New reporting suggests the PC version may arrive sooner than the 19-month gap between GTA 5’s console and PC releases.

items.title: The Elder Scrolls VI reportedly named Sentinel and set in Hammerfell
items.summary: Bethesda reportedly confirmed The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel and identified Hammerfell as its setting, while providing few additional details about the long-awaited RPG.

items.title: Xbox begins rollout of redesigned PC app
items.summary: Microsoft is rolling out a redesigned Xbox app to PC Xbox Insiders, claiming launch times up to 60% faster and loading times for key pages up to 50% faster.

items.title: Elevator Action arrives on PS5 and Switch 2
items.summary: Taito’s 1983 arcade classic Elevator Action is now available on PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 through the console archives.
